question.:question/problem:
A storage tank initially holds $600\,\text{L}$ of liquid containing $23\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved stabilizer.
A feed solution containing $0.04\,\text{kg/L}$ of the stabilizer is pumped into the tank at a rate of $15\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed liquid is drained out at a rate of $10\,\text{L/min}.$

$$\frac{dQ}{dt}=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}.$$
The units of these rates are $\text{kg/min}.$

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which substance enters the tank.
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{in}}&=(0.04\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot(15\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\\
&=(0.04\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(15\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.6\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$V(t)=600+15t-10t=(600+5t)\,\text{L}.$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{600+5t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(10\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{600+5t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(10\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{600+5t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{10Q}{600+5t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{2Q}{120+t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.6-\frac{2Q}{120+t}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus,
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{2}{120+t}Q=0.6.$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 2/(120+t)\,dt}\\&=e^{2\ln|120+t|}\\&=e^{\ln (120+t)^{2}}\\&=(120+t)^{2}.\end{aligned}$$

A fermentation vat initially holds $144\,\text{L}$ of liquid containing $8.64\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved nutrient.
A feed solution containing $0.06\,\text{kg/L}$ of the nutrient is pumped into the vat at a rate of $16\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed liquid is drained out at a rate of $8\,\text{L/min}.$
Find, rounded to two decimal places, the amount of nutrient in the vat $15$ minutes after pumping begins.

Let $Q$ be the amount of dissolved substance in the tank at time $t,$ in minutes. The amount entering minus the amount leaving gives
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}.$$
The units of these rates are $\text{kg/min}.$

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which substance enters the tank.
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{in}}&=(0.06\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot(16\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\\
&=(0.06\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot(16\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\\&=0.96\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which substance exits the tank.
The volume is
$$V(t)=144+16t-8t=(144+8t)\,\text{L}.$$
The concentration is $\frac{Q}{144+8t}\,\text{kg/L}.$ Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}Q'_{\text{out}}&=(8\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{144+8t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\\
&=(8\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot(\frac{Q}{144+8t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\\
&=\frac{8Q}{144+8t}\,\text{kg/min}=\frac{1Q}{18+t}\,\text{kg/min}.\end{aligned}$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=Q'_{\text{in}}-Q'_{\text{out}}\\&=0.96-\frac{1Q}{18+t}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus,
$$\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{18+t}Q=0.96.$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.
This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:
$$\begin{aligned}I(t)&=e^{\int 1/(18+t)\,dt}\\&=e^{1\ln|18+t|}\\&=e^{\ln (18+t)^{1}}\\&=(18+t)^{1}.\end{aligned}$$
Multiplying both sides by $I(t)=(18+t)^{1}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}(18+t)^{1}\cdot(\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{1}{18+t}Q)&=(18+t)^{1}\cdot 0.96\\
(18+t)^{1}\frac{dQ}{dt}+1(18+t)^{0}Q&=0.96(18+t)^{1}\\\frac{d}{dt}(Q(18+t)^{1})&=0.96(18+t)^{1}.\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\int\frac{d}{dt}(Q(18+t)^{1})\,dt&=\int 0.96(18+t)^{1}\,dt\\Q(18+t)^{1}&=0.96\cdot\frac{1}{2}(18+t)^{2}+C\\Q(t)&=0.48(18+t)+C(18+t)^{-1}.\end{aligned}$$
